blocks.text: SPDT Micro Limit Switch Short Roller Lever 13mm 16A

The SPDT Micro Limit Switch with short roller lever is a compact, robust snap-action switch designed to sense or limit mechanical movement in a variety of devices. Its small rectangular body houses an internal mechanism that can rapidly toggle contacts as soon as the roller lever is actuated. The short roller lever arm (about 13 mm) makes the switch especially useful where space is limited or where only small movement is expected enabling precise detection or control of mechanical travel without bulky hardware.

Despite its small size, this limit switch supports a relatively high current rating (16 A), so it combines modest physical footprint with serious switching capability. The roller lever allows actuation through gentle contact or slight motion, reducing the force or displacement required to trigger the switch useful when used to detect small shifts or the presence/absence of moving parts. Because the switch is “SPDT” (single pole double throw), it offers flexibility to switch between normally-closed (NC) and normally-open (NO) circuits, making it adaptable to many control logic schemes.

Overall, the Micro Limit Switch Short Roller Lever 13mm 16A provides a reliable, snap-action solution for mechanical position detection, end-of-travel sensing, or limit detection in electromechanical systems. Its durable build, compact lever design, and high current capacity make it a practical component for appliances, machinery, or DIY electrical/electronic projects where space constraints and dependable switching matter. It is a good choice whenever you need a straightforward, low-profile mechanical switch that can reliably endure repeated operations.

blocks.text: MAX712CPE+ Multi-Chemical 1~16 P DIP-16 Battery Management IC

The MAX712CPE+ is a specialized integrated circuit designed to manage the fast charging of Nickel-Metal Hydride (NiMH) and Nickel-Cadmium (NiCd) battery packs. It operates as a sophisticated controller that regulates the charging process from a DC power source, ensuring batteries are charged efficiently and safely. The chip is capable of handling battery configurations ranging from 1 to 16 cells connected in series, making it highly versatile for various battery-powered devices.

The primary role of the MAX712 is to conduct a constant-current fast-charge cycle, which can occur at rates as high as 4C. Its intelligent charging algorithm determines when the battery is fully charged by monitoring multiple parameters. Unlike the MAX713 which detects a negative voltage slope, the MAX712 is designed to terminate the fast charge upon detecting a zero voltage slope (∆V/∆t=0). It also incorporates temperature window comparators and a programmable timer as backup termination methods to prevent overcharging.

Housed in a standard 16-pin PDIP package, the device is powered through an on-board 5V shunt regulator from the DC input. It features a low-side current-sense resistor, allowing it to regulate the charge current even while simultaneously powering the system’s load from the same source. When not actively charging, the IC draws a minimal current of only 5µA from the battery, preserving its charge. It can be configured for either linear or more efficient switch-mode power control.

blocks.text: The 10pF 50V ceramic capacitor is a small through-hole capacitor used in high-frequency and timing circuits. Very low values like 10pF are typical around crystals and oscillators, in RF and antenna circuits, and for filtering fast noise on signal lines. Ceramic capacitors are non-polarized, so they can be fitted either way round.
Typical marking: 100 (10 followed by no zeros = 10pF)

Ceramic capacitors use a three-digit code in picofarads: the first two digits are the value and the third digit is the number of zeros. So 100 means 10pF, 220 means 22pF and 104 means 100,000pF (100nF).

A crystal oscillator usually has one capacitor from each crystal pin to GND. Two 10pF capacitors in this position give 10 × 10 ÷ (10 + 10) = 5pF, plus a few pF of board stray capacitance, which suits crystals specified for a load of about 8pF to 10pF. Always check the load capacitance in your crystal’s datasheet; many 16 MHz Arduino crystals use 22pF instead.

blocks.text: This clear plastic storage box offers up to 18 compartments with removable dividers, so you can adjust the grid sizes to fit your parts. It is ideal for sorting electronic components, screws and small hardware, and the transparent body shows every compartment at a glance. Two front snap latches keep the lid firmly closed when you carry the box.
Dividers: removable, for adjustable compartment sizes
Resistors, capacitors, LEDs, diodes and transistors
ICs, headers, connectors and jumper wires
Remove dividers to make larger compartments for modules, cables or tools, and keep the small grids for resistors and tiny parts.
Label each compartment with the part value so you find what you need quickly.
Store static-sensitive ICs in anti-static foam or bags inside their compartment.
Close both latches before carrying the box so parts do not jump between compartments.
Electronic component storage for makers, students and technicians
Screw and hardware sorting in the workshop
Ready project kits for classes and workshops
